title: Tabi
summary: One place for the plan, the people and the money. A phone-first group trip planner.
caption: Public sign-in screen. Trip and account data remain private.
goal: Support different trips, group sizes and budgets without clutter, while keeping confirmed spending distinct from estimates.
contributions: Designed and built multi-trip accounts, invite-only groups and viewer/editor roles.
Built the day-by-day itinerary, map pins, budget views and budget-ceiling warning.
Integrated currency conversion, weather and a home view that changes during a trip.
Iterated on the code and visual design for a mobile-first, phone-app feel.
systems: Itinerary and map pins for each day.
Paid, committed and estimated costs remain distinct.
process: A Japan trip provided the first real use. Later iterations broadened the product for different trips and groups, with repeated passes on the code and interface.
testing: [CONTENT NEEDED] Add anonymised usability notes and a before/after screen comparison.
result: A live, invite-only web app. The public link opens its sign-in screen.
decision: Paid, committed and estimated costs are separate states: a guess should never read as money already spent. The home view changes from a countdown before the trip to today’s plan during it.
reflection: The project demonstrates product thinking alongside implementation: permissions, financial clarity and information hierarchy all affect how useful the same data is on a phone.
